chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), peace be upon him, said:
I asked him about the man who eats with his left hand or drinks with it, so he said: 'He should not eat with his left hand, nor drink with his left hand, nor take anything with it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating and drinking with the left hand according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the etiquette of eating by prohibiting the use of the left hand not only for consuming food and drink but also for general handling of items, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on bodily purity and following the Prophet’s Sunnah. This ruling is often interpreted by scholars as either a recommended act of worship (mustahabb) or a prohibition (nahy) depending on the context of other narrations, highlighting the left hand's traditional association with impurity in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who eats with his left hand, or drinks with it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not eat with his left hand, nor drink with his left hand, nor take anything with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who eats or drinks with his left hand.
He (the Imam) said, ‘He must not eat with his left hand and must not drink with his left hand or lift up anything with it.’”
